Bank of Albania Governor Ardian Fullani's word at meeting with teachers and high school students "Fuat Babeni" in Bilisht and "Raqi Qirinxhi" in Korca Publication date: 15.02.2009 Education costs but it's priceless! As can be understood by the saying behind me, today's meeting will cost him  1/5 05/08/22, 16:58 Mr Ardian Fullani, at the meeting with teachers and high school students "Fua... education. And where better could I have this conversation than in a high school class?! Of course, the theme of education is very broad, but as governor of the Bank of Albania I will discuss with you today on the education and formation of an economic-financial culture. I. Why should economic-financial education start early? Rightly many of you can judge that this kind of knowledge is benefited by experience, schooling and the passage of years. But believe me, based on studies even after 13 years of primary and secondary schooling, 4 years of university schooling and 2 years of postgraduate schooling, 2/3 of Americans of age could not answer the question: Whether the amount of goods purchased with a year's savings is the same, greater or less in conditions when the interest rate of the savings deposit has been 1 percent and annual inflation 2%. Studies have shown that even in pioneering countries of sophisticated financial products and services, the economic-financial culture of the population leaves to be desired. What indicates that financial economic education must start early. This is particularly necessary in places like ours, where for decades the state was the one that cared for the security of people's income. A good economic-financial education would enable the citizens of our country tomorrow not to step before simple questions such as: How is a credit card used? What benefit do I have from the compound interest? How can I invest my savings better? Why I need a fund pension? Without then affecting more complex macroeconomic issues such as supply and demand, overall production, the impact of monetary policy on everyone's lives, as well as many other problems of this nature. Can you imagine how much more effectively the decisions of the BSH Supervisory Council would be made to change interest rate if the public were better educated on how things work in a market economy? Consumer behaviour is also about correcting people's harmful tendencies. Trends that in most cases result from the lack of proper education of people in the field of finance. For this reason, we at the Bank of Albania like the philosophy of creating an economic-financial culture from a young age. Think for a moment how useful it would be in everyday life if a high school student who knows Victor Hygo's work, trigonometry and biology well doesn't know how to manage his money?! II. Central bank and economic-financial education. First I must say, that the central bank's commitment to economic and financial education to the public is related to achieving its basic goals. We are aware that an informed public, a public that understands our role in the economy, will be much better able to understand and accept the reasons behind the difficult decisions central bankers make from time to time. So for them to make sound financial decisions today that will lead to the smart use of money and the construction of economic well-being tomorrow. There are some approaches to economic-financial education. One approach is that direct, which teaches basic economic concepts. Another sees economic education as a community of knowledge about specific themes. Such a topic is the benefit of free trade or the globalization of the labour market. What would be the best approach? We at the Bank of Albania have wasted no time in answering a question that does not have a single, accurate answer. As the great English economist Alfred Marshall, who saw the economy as studying the financial behavior of people in everyday life (a study of mankind in the ordinary business of life), has tried to get the Central Bank closer to the daily life of the public. Like Marshall, we believe the best way to succeed is to help people understand the link between economics and everyday life. Albanian economy facing challenges of time Lecture by Bank of Albania Governor Ardian Fullani at the conference "Global Financial Crisis and Future Developments", organised by the Good Council Zoya University and the University of Bologna, March 27, 2009 Publication date: 30.03.2009  1/5 06/08/2022, 09:17 Lecture by Bank of Albania Governor Ardian Fullani at the conference "Global Financial Crisis and Developments of... Honored participants, It is special pleasure to be among you at this conference synthesized with the sharpest economic problems of the time, as well as to share with you some opinions about the performance of the Albanian economy and its confronting with the global financial crisis. Although its global origin is the same, the impact of this crisis is different in different countries, as does the nature of the problems and measures that have been presented for its solution. Fortunately, the Albanian economy is in a more comfortable position for its coping compared to many countries in the region or countries along the path of transition. I say fortunately, not to define the casual nature of the favourable economic and financial position in which we are located, but to highlight the fact that the country's consolidated macroeconomic balances enable us to have a reduced impact of the crisis and greater breathing on its treatment. In reality, there is nothing casual about our achievements towards the sustainable economic development of the country. The bank of Albania's attention, as one of the main actors in drafting and implementing economic policies, has been constantly oriented towards meeting this goal. Our efforts in this direction are also complemented by a healthy framework for coordinating macroeconomic policies, in which a non-small role has played imf assistance and the financial support it has enabled. All these premises have caused the Albanian economy to grow at satisfactory pace over the last decade, marking GDP growth of an average of 5-6 percent per year. Nominal per capita income has almost tripled over the past 8 years, while low inflation has led to this increase directly translating into increased well-being. On the other hand, fiscal policy has been relatively cautious. Its traits have been contoured by the need to maintain fiscal discipline, expressed this in the care of controlling the budget deficit, public debt and the government's impact in internal financial markets. Like many other developing countries, our economic growth has been associated with high levels of the trade deficit. These deficits are financed by stable capital inflows in the form of remittances or foreign direct investment. However, the economy's performance during the last quarter of 2008 and the first months of 2009 is witnessing an increasing impact of the global financial crisis on the country's economy. Briefly, this impact is illustrated in the decline in remittances and imports, tightening liquidity conditions and lower credit growth, as well as increasing the uncertainty of economic agents. All these developments have prompted a public debate on taking action to cope with them, as well as highlighting the need for coordination of the efforts of all economic actors in the country. The financial system has been an important factor in supporting the country's high economic growth. It has shown a steady increase in activity, especially in recent years. This development is supported by continued reforms aimed at increasing competition and continuously improving regulatory and supervisory infrastructure. Today, the entire banking sector is owned by private equity and most banks are owned by ankeks_ise_Shqiperisek_z_Aridianb_Fullkani_nej_... 2/5 06/08/2022, 09:17 Lecture by Bank of Albania Governor Ardian Fullani at the conference "Global Financial Crisis and Developments of... well-known European banking groups. In the last 5 years, the banking sector's active expanded by 15 20 percent per year on average, rising to 87 percent of the country's GDP, late 2008. As a result, in the last four years credit for the economy has increased on average by 7 percentage points against GDP, rising to 37 percent of GDP. Regulatory and supervisory infrastructure of the financial system has also improved. Within the framework of the regulatory and supervisory role of banking activity, the Bank of Albania has aimed to implement the best international standards. The aim is for banking activity and banks to develop in a balanced manner and with known and controlled risks. For this reason, the Bank of Albania has concluded that any development, which is generally perceived as positive for banking activity and the economy in general, can be accompanied by added risks in the direction of the financial stability of the system. Our objective is to be precursors in the direction of identifying and taking measures to precede the materialization of these risks in the future. To be a little more concrete, I am referring to the rapid growth in lending of the banking sector. We were dealing with positive development in support of the country's economic development, but the Bank of Albania could not neglect for any moment the other side of the medal, the quality of the portfolio. The same is true as to the composition of the loan portfolio according to the currencies. The prevalence of currency loans makes the loan portfolio sensitive to the performance of the local currency exchange rate against the main currencies. To ensure the best management of these risks on the part of The banking sector, the Bank of Albania in recent years has taken various regulatory actions to better discipline the rapid growth of credit, as well as to establish a better balance of the composition of the loan portfolio according to currencies. Even over the past year, the performance of the banking sector was generally positive. Banking activity was presented well-capitalised and secular. The capital sufficiency index resulted in 17.2 percent, while the banking sector's assets represented 43 percent of the banking sector's total active. However, due to developments in the international crisis, in the last quarter of the year the banking sector faced an unstable situation of public deposit performance, which over the past year grew only 2 percent. The low pace of growth dictated a slowdown in the banking sector's annual active growth to 12.3 percent, as well as slowing lending activity to 35 percent. Slowing profitable activities, as well as rising activity costs, affected the decline in the positive outcome of banking activity. The banking sector's profit for 2008 was about 7.3 billion dollars. Under these conditions, the Bank of Albania took several actions aimed at explaining in public, professionally and as clearly as possible the effects of the international crisis, through the presence in the media and the increase in the number of various publications; strengthening control over banking activity through expanding reporting requirements and increasing controls in the country; strengthening dialogue with the banking industry; strengthening co-operation with other supervisory authorities in the country as well as in the region; improving the regulatory framework in certain directions of banking activity; preparing measures aimed at maintaining public confidence in the banking sector, including the proposal for increasing the value of deposit insurance. The Bank of Albania, assessing its role, has contributed to maintaining liquidity in the  3/5 06/08/2022, 09:17 Lecture by Bank of Albania Governor Ardian Fullani at the conference "Global Financial Crisis and Developments of... The Bank of Albania, assessing its role, has contributed to maintaining liquidity in the optimal levels, mainly through an effective combination of operational instruments that she has available. The Bank of Albania has successfully alternated the injection of liquidity into interbank market, through week-long mutual repurchase agreements at price fixed with longer-term injection options, including right-to-sell operations full. 2009 is expected to be a tougher year for increasing banking activity. But the banking sector will be stable, in the conditions of maintaining satisfactory levels of activity capitalisation and actions to preserve liquidity indicators. The Bank of Albania has requested maximum commitment and care from banking industry representatives to monitor and cope with developments this year. We have sought to strengthen the control of the banks' management structures, over the activity of their institutions. This must be done in line with the need to adapt to the added requirements for information on the part of the Bank of Albania, for real-time recognition of developments in banking activity. Specifically, the Bank of Albania has asked bank shareholders to be willing to add capital in case of need and preserve funding lines for their subsidiaries operating in Albania. Within the parameters of a secure banking activity and in accordance with the requirements of the supervisory regulatory framework, the banking sector must exploit existing opportunities to carry out its important role in financial mediation and in supporting the country's economic growth. Let me present some milestones that guide the Bank of Albania's analysis and decision-making in the current situation. As is clear to any economic researcher, the development of any cell of economic activity must be known and face its budgetary constraints. This applies not only to separate companies or the family budget, but also to the economy as a whole. The challenges facing the country in the future are precisely to reduce the opportunities for financing economic activity. Due to problems that originate mainly outside Albania, the opportunities for financing the banking system are more reduced than a year ago. Balances of the banking system, although healthy and well-capitalized, are characterized by a lower level of liquidity. Similarly, understandably, the banking system's care for the quality of the loan portfolio has increased significantly, bringing about a further reduction in the bank loan offer. In the absence of foreign financial resources, it is normal for the Albanian economy to be aware and accept these financial constraints over the short term. Albanian business and consumers should be more careful in using banking system funds. This is not a call for contracting bank borrowing, but a signal for increasing efficiency in the use of disposable funds. This concern should be recognised and welcomed by all economic, public or private agents. Economic development is a constant showdown of desires for lending stimulus in support of investment consumption and economic growth with the needs for a sustainable  4/5 06/08/2022, 09:17 Lecture by Bank of Albania Governor Ardian Fullani at the conference "Global Financial Crisis and Developments of... support for consumption, investment and economic growth, with the needs for a sustainable macroeconomic balances. The latter, condition the pace of growth of the economy, in one long-term period. Strong stimulus policies could buy economic growth for a short period of time. But this strategy would damage long-term price stability, eroding the purchasing power of the economy and losing confidence in the national currency and financial institutions. Also, these measures could result in a balance sheet deficit payments, causing strong economic contractions in a second period. In a way Clearly, such an economic strategy would result in counterproductive. All this trouble, supports the Bank of Albania's opinion that the preservation of macroeconomic stability, expressed in the low inflation, healthy public and private balances, fiscal debt sustainability and foreign currency position of the economy as well as in low fluctuating financial markets, It is the right key to orienting and developing our economic policies.  5/5

Ardian Fullani, n konferencn "Kriza financiare globale dhe zhvillimet e a T nderuar pjesmarrs, sht knaqsi e veant t jem mes jush n kt konferenc t sintonizuar me problemet m t mprehta ekonomike t kohs, si dhe t ndaj me ju disa opinione n lidhje me ecurin e ekonomis shqiptare dhe prballjen e saj me krizn financiare botrore. Ndonse origjina e saj globale sht e njjt, ndikimi i ksaj krize sht i ndryshm n vende t ndryshme, ashtu si ndryshon edhe natyra e problemeve dhe masave q jan parashtruar pr zgjidhjen e saj. Fatmirsisht, ekonomia shqiptare gjendet n nj pozicion m komod pr prballimin e saj krahasuar me shum vende t rajonit apo vende bashkudhtare n rrugn e tranzicionit. Them fatmirsisht, jo pr t prkufizuar natyrn rastsore t pozicionit t favorshm ekonomik dhe financiar n t cilin ndodhemi, por pr t theksuar faktin q ekuilibrat e konsoliduar makroekonomik t vendit na mundsojn nj ndikim m t reduktuar t krizs dhe nj frymmarrje m t madhe n trajtimin e saj. N realitet, nuk ka asgj rastsore n arritjet tona drejt zhvillimit t qndrueshm ekonomik t vendit. Vmendja e Banks s Shqipris, si nj nga aktort kryesor n hartimin dhe zbatimin e politikave ekonomike, ka qen vazhdimisht e orientuar drejt prmbushjes s ktij synimi. Prpjekjet tona n kt drejtim jan plotsuar edhe nga nj kuadr i shndetshm pr koordinimin e politikave makroekonomike, n t cilin nj rol jo t vogl ka luajtur asistenca e FMN-s dhe mbshtetja financiare q ajo ka mundsuar. T gjitha kto premisa, kan br q ekonomia shqiptare t rritet me ritme t knaqshme gjat dekads s fundit, duke shnuar rritje t PBB-s prej mesatarisht 5-6 pr qind n vit. T ardhurat nominale pr frym jan pothuajse trefishuar gjat 8 viteve t fundit, ndrkoh q inflacioni i ult ka br q kjo rritje t prkthehet direkt n rritje t mirqenies. Nga ana tjetr, politika fiskale ka qen relativisht e kujdesshme. Tiparet e saj jan konturuar nga nevoja pr ruajtjen e disiplins fiskale, e shprehur kjo n kujdesin pr kontrollin e deficitit buxhetor, t borxhit publik dhe t impaktit t qeveris n tregjet e brendshme financiare. Ashtu si dhe shum vende t tjera n zhvillim, rritja jon ekonomike sht shoqruar me nivele t larta t deficitit tregtar. Kto deficite jan financuar nga hyrjet e qndrueshme t kapitalit n formn e remitancave apo t investimeve t huaja direkte. Megjithat, ecuria e ekonomis gjat tremujorit t fundit t vitit 2008 dhe muajve t par t vitit 2009, po dshmon nj ndikim gjithnj e m t madh t krizs financiare botrore n ekonomin e vendit. Shkurtimisht, ky ndikim ilustrohet n rnien e remitancave dhe t importeve, n shtrngimin e kushteve t likuiditetit dhe rritjen m t ult t kredis, si dhe n rritjen e pasiguris s agjentve ekonomik. T gjitha kto zhvillime, kan nxitur nj debat publik pr marrjen e masave pr prballimin e tyre, si dhe kan nxjerr n pah nevojn pr koordinimin e prpjekjeve t t gjith aktorve ekonomik t vendit. Sistemi financiar ka qen nj faktor i rndsishm n mbshtetjen e rritjes s lart ekonomike t vendit. Ai ka shfaqur nj rritje t qndrueshme t veprimtaris, veanrisht kto vitet e fundit. Ky zhvillim sht mbshtetur nga reforma t vazhdueshme t cilat kan synuar rritjen e konkurrencs dhe prmirsimin e vazhdueshm t infrastrukturs rregullative dhe mbikqyrse. Title: Speech at the press conference for the Financial Stability Report 2008
text: Mr. Ardian Fullani, in pr... Annual port for 2008 to the Assembly of Albania, 16 April 2009 29/07/22, 14:58 Mr Ardian Fullani, at the presentation of the 2008 Annual Report to the Assembly of Albania, 16 April 2009 Publication date: 16.04.2009 Honorable, Mrs. Speaker! Honourable deputies! In accordance with the legal obligation it is a special honour and privilege to present before you the bank of Albania's report on its activity exercised in 2008. I take advantage of this occasion to express my thanks for the support and understanding that the Assembly of Albania has given to the institution I lead. 2008 faced a complex situation on the global plain. Especially starting in September, a string of previously unlived events rocked U.S. financial infrastructure. The major integration of the financial market had enabled the distribution of infected products throughout the developed world, including the growing economies of Asia. Soon, the world economy found itself in general confusion as a result of which the public's confidence in the financial system was severely damaged. Prices in all major stock exchanges began to fall rapidly, while larger banks reported significant losses. Many financial institutions with centuries-old history collapsed, forcing authorities to take a series of rescue actions. The governments and central banks of developed countries, including specialised international bodies, adopted a series of emergency measures. With the aim of returning public confidence to the banking system, in addition to injecting liquidity, capital injection or buying of infected assets through public funds was considered reasonable. Page 1 of 13 Mr. Ardian Fullani, in pr... Annual port for 2008 to the Assembly of Albania, 16 April 2009 29/07/22, 14:58 Globalisation of the crisis severely damaged world trade by spreading rapidly in developing and low-income countries. Developing countries are experiencing a deterioration in financial conditions, tightening lending, exchange rate pressures, and at the same time significant declines in demand for highly important branches of economic activity. In late 2008 and early 2009, some of the developing countries, new members of the European Union, suffered heavy blows. Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Baltic countries, including other states such as Ukraine, Serbia, Belarus and others, faced with a general balance of payment crisis, turned to the International Monetary Fund for immediate assistance. The end of 2008 and January 2009 finally confirmed the contracting of economic activity in the economies of the US, Germany, Italy, Britain and Japan. International markets continue to fluctuate significantly by adding uncertainty and uncertainty among participants in them. The future still remains with many questions despite numerous efforts on the global plain. Such an effort was also the London meeting where the leaders of the 20 most developed countries decided to create a US1.1 trillion fund to stimulate economic activity on a global scale, including help for poor countries through strengthening the role of the International Monetary Fund. The situation I described above leaves you to understand the great pressure that the global economy in general generates and that of partner countries in particular, on our country's still fragile economy. In my public appearances, in press releases of the Supervisory Council of the Bank of Albania as well as in other official documents of the institution, international developments and the complications they can cause in the activity of our economy have been discussed. In general, the Albanian economy has shown a high degree of resistance to phenomena that characterized global developments in the last quarter of 2008. High immunity also showed the Albanian banking system, which showed no signs of panic and confusion. Some experts have praised Albania as a lucky country, while some others have found the cause for a small integration of the Albanian economy with the global economy. The Bank of Albania thinks the main reason has to do with the great attention we have devoted in recent years to the financial stability of the banking system. The Albanian economy is integrated as much as other Balkan economies are integrated, some of which have already surrendered. Let me take this statement a little further. The Albanian banking system can be considered an extension of the banking system of the most developed European countries. About 80 percent of the system's active people belong to banking groups that have headquarters in Eurozone countries, moreover extended throughout our wider region. The extent of the same banking groups in many countries caused lending policies, deposit collection, to be similar for all these countries. As a result, exposure to the risks these policies imposed was the same as for Albania, as was albania. Page 2 of 13 Mr. Ardian Fullani, in pr... Annual port for 2008 to the Assembly of Albania, 16 April 2009 29/07/22, 14:58 Bulgaria, Romania or Serbia. In this respect, it can be said that the country's financial integration has been the same as other countries in the region in terms of the number of operators, their type and the products they offered. Like most other countries, Albania had the next promotion when in 2006 one of the known agencies rated Albania with the B1 rating, which was the same for 2008. A similar assessment has been for other countries in the region, causing the country's risk perception on the part of foreign investors to be more or less the same. This is also confirmed by the purchase of internal debt from foreign financial institutions. In addition, I would like to stress that even actions in capital accounts, especially from the perspective of foreign investors, are entirely liberalized, creating no obstacles to the entry and exit of capital. The increase in foreign transactions is another indicator about the scale of the country's openness to the rest of the world. Exports and imports have recorded high rates year-on-year, causing the country's trade activity to increase significantly. About 80 per cent of this trade activity takes place with Eurozone countries, where as key partners Italy and Greece. The strong deepening of the trade deficit from one year to the next was a typical sign of the so-called rapid approximation process. This phenomenon has been the main characteristic of the development of all Eastern European countries that have joined the EU in recent years, including most southwestern Balkan countries, where our country is also a part. The arguments I put forward above believe that they are sufficient to understand that we have been neither lucky nor undeveloped or on the sidelines of global developments. What has distinguished the Albanian financial system from a range of systems of countries in the region have been its performance and health indicators, which are largely owed to the work and measures of the Bank of Albania. The policies and decisions we have adopted in recent years have taken the form of various platforms to carefully manage the situations we have faced over time. In my assessment I would like to stress that the decisions made, from 2006 to 2006 In August 2008, in the field of monetary policy and banking supervision, they created the immunity platform. Decisions adopted in autumn 2008 to the present day constitute the platform of absorbing the effects of the crisis. At the same time, the Bank of Albania is working intensively on the third platform: the Revitalization Platform. Let me be honoured to stop briefly on each of the three platforms I mentioned above. Immunity Platform In a general context I appreciate that the immunity of our economy concerns the large savings of Albanians, materialized in the form of deposits and in the determination of the Bank of Albania to administratively prohibit the penetration of certain products, which in other countries have resulted in fatal. In a more analytical perspective I am stopping at our shares in the past, which I Page 3 of 13 Mr. Ardian Fullani, in pr... Annual port for 2008 to the Assembly of Albania, 16 April 2009 29/07/22, 14:58 I value as immunization therapy to current developments. First, I want to bring to your attention monetary policy decisions in the period July 2006 November 2007, during which the basic interest rate increased five fold reaching the 6.25 percent level. This level remained unchanged during 2008. Our main motivation was related to the overheating of the economy, which mainly reflected the large increase in domestic demand as a result of credit expansion for the economy. Today, the Bank of Albania estimates that tightening monetary policy has been an effective buffer in controlling domestic demand in the economy, directly affecting the credit channel for the economy. Overall, the Bank of Albania estimates that the overall macroeconomic environment has been healthy for the past four years, including 2008. By making a summary analysis of these developments, although we are still awaiting confirmations from official statistics, the Bank of Albania considers that the country's economy has grown in line with early forecasts. This growth has reflected the dynamic development of several sectors of the economy, supported by increased consumption and investment in the economy, as well as continued structural and infrastructural improvements of the economy. Economic growth in the country is mainly based on rapid growth in domestic demand, which remains the main generator of economic growth. Consumption, investment and government spending marked increases during 2008. External demand in the form of exports has marked rapid growth in recent years, but it still remains at low levels to support the country's economic growth. Economic activity in the country is financed mainly by internal sources. Thanks to its high liquidity during 2008, the Albanian banking system has been able to respond to the demand for funds of the economy with increased financial mediation. During 2008, the bank loan portfolio increased by 7.3 percentage points of GDP. The Bank of Albania has met its legal objective of maintaining price stability in the economy. The average annual inflation rate marked the 3.4 percent value during 2008, being close enough to the Bank of Albania's target of 3 percent and within our tolerance interval of 2-4 percent. The controlled level of inflation reflects the appropriate monetary conditions and fair monetary policy of the Bank of Albania. The latter has made it possible to balance demand and supply factors, as well as to anchor inflationary expectations about the Bank of Albania's target. Fiscal policy has had a more expansionist character during 2008. The budget deficit for 2008 is estimated to have reached 5.7 percent of GDP, deepening by about 2.2 percentage points in annual terms. The level of public debt marked increases during 2008, reaching 55.6 percent of GDP from 52.2 percent a year earlier. Improving public debt management in the direction of extending the maturity deadline and diversifying funding resources is positive development that has helped refinance debt and control its cost impact in budget indicators. Third, I would like to emphasize the sensitivity shown and the adjustments made in the area of banking supervision during this period. In 2006, for the first time, the Bank of Albania's annual conference was devoted entirely to the problems of financial stability seen from a regional point of view. On 1 June 2007, the Banks in the Republic of Albania law came into force, which presents the first phase of the extermination of Albanian legislation with acquis communautaire in accordance with the commitments undertaken in the Stabilisation Association Agreement. In this act, internal control is considered an integral part of the governance of banks. For this reason, basic principles for independent, impartial and responsible control are sanctioned in regulation. To this end, the Bank of Albania values the quality of human resources essentially, implying the recruitment of professionals in decision-making and risk management. At the end of this uninterrupted process of co-operation and investigation we have reached conclusions, which have often put us in positions of confrontation with ideas and practices contrary to our own. The fruit of this process was our insistence on administratively stopping the crediting of the economy with so-called exotic money. In recent years it has become fashionable lending in the Swiss or Japanese currency, funds which for the time represented loans at very cheap costs, ready to penetrate even our economy. As long as this activity was deemed high risk, under conditions when credit beneficiaries or banks did not create adequate protection, it was not reasonable to administratively block the granting of loans on the part of the banking system to customers, in these two types of currencies. I think that way we have contributed directly to curbing short-term capital inflows from mother banks to daughter banks, in the form of credit lines. Let me remember that many of the developing economies have fallen into the trap of these funds, which today are seriously suffering from the need to refinance debts in these currencies. Crisis Absorption Platform The outbreak of the financial crisis in autumn 2008 spread to many countries of the world as a crisis of confidence, also had its impact on the Albanian banking system. Faced with a reasonable reluctance of individuals, the banking system faced a flow of deposits throughout the period October 2008. However, very good capitalization and satisfactory liquidity situation enabled us to cope with this situation. Currently, the Albanian economy is increasingly coming under pressure from the global crisis. The uncertainty that conveyed the shock of the global financial system as I explained above was reflected in the withdrawal of a portion of deposits from the system, bringing liquidity problems and tendencies to raise interest rates. This situation has naturally influenced the reduction of the system's opportunity and readiness to credit the economy. On the other hand, developments in the global economy suggest that the Albanian economy will face a reduction in currency flows during 2009. These developments constitute a further reduction in economic activity financing opportunities, as well as damage the balances of demand and currency supply. They have been associated with the birth of derogatory pressures on the exchange rate, as have the economies of many other Eastern European countries. In itself, this understatement, under the conditions of the flexible exchange rate regime that applies in Albania constitutes correctional behaviour towards consumption, savings and investments at the micro and macroeconomic level. As we have stressed in our other public appearances, this restriction must be recognised and factored into the business plans of all economic agents. The Albanian economy will benefit less credit during 2009. This lack of liquidity also limits the spaces that fiscal and monetary policies have for action. Under these circumstances, what is required is a greater efficiency of the use of banking system funds, through the priority ranking of expenditures in the function of the pact that have on economic growth. Over time, following the situation step by step, the Bank of Albania modified its operational framework to better meet the market's liquidity needs. Initially we have changed the type of main injection auction, from multi-fixed auction to fixed-price auction, which means supplying the market with liquidity in the amount banks deem reasonable themselves and all this, versus the fixed price of the basic interest percentage. Through a separate regulatory act, the Bank of Albania has urged the banking sector not to distribute the 2008 profit in the form of a dividend. In this way, the capitalization of banking activity is further strengthened, providing one more guarantee for the financial health of the banking sector, following. Revitalization Platform The current problems facing the Albanian economy have not originated in Albania; For this reason, their solution will depend to a large extent on improving economic activity at the world level. The future development strategy must continue to rely on the fundamental elements I outlined on the first platform. Macroeconomic stability will remain a fundamental prerequisite for sustainable long-term growth. Based on the lessons of the global crisis, the Bank of Albania considers it vital to look beyond today and further deepen structural reforms. This also constitutes the main condition for the country's stable convergence with European Union standards. By assessing the complexity of the challenges we will face next, we judge as fundamental the revision of all current macroeconomic and financial policies with the aim of adapting them to the new conditions. Tightening financial conditions in the economy, insufficiency of internal resources and problems of the international financial market make it necessary to find foreign sources of financing. To this end, every possible option, including support programmes by specialized international institutions, should be evaluated. The Bank of Albania considers that Albania should always benefit from the international fund created by the collection of the twenty most developed countries, as it meets all conditions. On behalf of the institution I lead I would like to assure the Assembly of Albania, the banking system, all other actors interested that the Bank of Albania will meet the needs of the banking system with liquidity. On the other hand, we will insist that the banking system in the policies it applies in relation to the money market and investment portfolio be more independent of headquarters. The Bank of Albania will intensify communication with banks' headquarters to financially support their daughters operating in Albania. Banks operating in Albania have been licensed and manage the savings of Albanian citizens. Consequently, the fundamental responsibility of any banking system is financial mediation in the country where it operates. For this reason, we will insist that the lending of the economy be revived by bringing to the attention of the system the particular branches of production that justify its financial support. The banking system must be more active in regaining public confidence, through increased communication and presentation of new products that address public hesitation. The business community needs to open up more to the banking system. Ashtu si e kemi theksuar edhe n dalje tona t tjera publike, ky kufizim duhet t njihet dhe t faktorizohet n planet e biznesit t t gjith agjentve ekonomik. Ekonomia shqiptare do t prfitoj m pak kredi gjat vitit 2009. Kjo munges likuiditeti kufizon edhe hapsirat q ka politika fiskale dhe ajo monetare pr veprim. N kto rrethana, ajo q krkohet sht nj eficienc m e madhe e prdorimit t fondeve t sistemit bankar, nprmjet renditjes prioritare t shpenzimeve n funksion t impaktit q kan mbi rritjen ekonomike. Pr m tepr, Banka e Shqipris gjykon se sjellja e deficitit t llogaris korente duhet t monitorohet n mnyr t vazhdueshme. Barazimi i ktij deficiti me hyrjet e reduktuara t llogaris kapitale, duhet t jet nj prioritet tjetr i zhvillimit t politikave ekonomike. Sikurse e theksova dhe m par, ky moment kushtzon ndjeshm ekuilibrat makroekonomik dhe financiar t vendit. Pr kt arsye, ai do t jet n vmendjen e vazhdueshme t analizs s Banks s Shqipris. Duke kuptuar drejt rolin e saj si nj institucion q administron tregun e paras, situatn e likuiditetit, stabilitetin e sistemit bankar dhe funksionin e saj si financuese e burimit t fundit, Banka e Shqipris q n ditt e para t tetorit 2008 bri publik qndrimin e saj se do t furnizonte sistemin bankar n mnyr t pandrprer me likuiditetin e nevojshm. Me kalimin e kohs, duke ndjekur situatn hap pas hapi, Banka e Shqipris modifikoi kuadrin e saj operacional pr t prmbushur m mir nevojat e tregut pr likuiditet. Fillimisht ne kemi ndryshuar tipin e ankandit kryesor t injektimit, nga ankand me shum fikse n ankand me mim fiks, q do t thot furnizim i tregut me likuiditet n sasin q bankat e gjykojn vet t arsyeshme dhe e gjith kjo, kundrejt mimit fiks t prqindjes baz t interesit. N shtes, Banka e Shqipris bri dhe disa modifikime t rndsishme rregullative. M konkretisht: U zgjerua baza e letrave me vler q shrbejn si kolateral pr marrveshjet e anasjellta t riblerjes, duke shtuar edhe obligacionet e emetuara nga qeveria, me maturim t mbetur jo m shum se 365 dit. U rrit hapsira e prdorimit t rezervs s detyruar nga 20 pr qind n 40 pr qind n dit. U ul diferenca midis norms baz t interesit t Banks s Shqipris dhe kredis njditore, nga 175 pik baz n vetm 75 pik. Nprmjet nj akti t veant rregullativ, Banka e Shqipris i ka krkuar sektorit bankar t mos shprndaj fitimin e vitit 2008, n formn e dividentit. Banka e Shqipris ka kryer testime t njpasnjshme, pr t gjetur reagimin e sistemit bankar n qoft se ai do t prballej me rrethana nga m ekstremet. Analizat e prftuara nga stress-test e shumta n rang sistemi ashtu dhe n mnyr individuale pr do bank m vete, tregojn se sistemi n trsi dhe asnj nga bankat me rndsi sistemike n veanti, nuk jan t prekura n nivelin e likuiditetit dhe t kapitalizimit. Pavarsisht zgjerimit t spektrit t rreziqeve dhe nj viti m t vshtir pr zgjerimin e veprimtaris bankare, sistemi financiar dhe sektori bankar do t mbeten t qndrueshm. Ne besojm q vendimi i fundit i Kuvendit t Shqipris i cili miratoi rritjen e vlers s plot t garantimit t depozitave n 2.5 milion lek, krijon t gjitha kushtet dhe eliminon barrierat psikologjike pr kthimin m t shpejt t depozitave t trhequra n sistemin bankar. Niveli aktual i sigurimit t depozitave, i ngjashm me at t vendeve evropiane, garanton plotsisht dhe prgjithmon kursimet e shumics drrmuese t familjeve shqiptare. Tashm nuk ka arsye objektive q njerzit t shqetsohen pr sigurin e kursimeve t tyre n banka. do hezitim pr t vendosur kursimet n banka, rrit n mnyr t panevojshme vlern e t ardhurave t munguara pr shkak t mosprfitimit t interesave dhe t shrbimeve t tjera bankare. Platforma e Rigjallrimit Problemet aktuale me t cilat prballet ekonomia shqiptare nuk kan origjinuar n Shqipri; pr kt arsye, zgjidhja e tyre do t varet n nj mas t madhe nga prmirsimi i aktivitetit ekonomik n nivel botror. Strategjia e ardhme e zhvillimit duhet t vazhdoj t mbshtetet n elementet fondamentale q shtjellova n platformn e par. Stabiliteti makroekonomik do t mbetet nj parakusht themelor pr nj rritje t qndrueshme afatgjat. Mbshtetur n msimet e deritanishme t krizs botrore, Banka e Shqipris gjykon jetike hedhjen e vshtrimit prtej t sotmes dhe thellimin e mtejshm t reformave strukturore. Kjo prbn dhe kushtin kryesor pr konvergimin e qndrueshm t vendit me standardet e Bashkimit Evropian. Shtrngimi i kushteve financiare n ekonomi, pamjaftueshmria e burimeve t brendshme dhe problemet e tregut financiar ndrkombtar, e bjn t nevojshme gjetjen e burimeve t huaja t financimit. Pr kt qllim, duhet vlersuar do opsion i mundshm, prfshir dhe programet e mbshtetjes nga institucionet ndrkombtare t specializuara. Banka e Shqipris gjykon se Shqipria duhet t prfitoj medoemos nga fondi ndrkombtar i krijuar nga mbledhja e njzet vendeve m t zhvilluara, pasi ajo i plotson t gjitha kushtet. N emr t institucionit q un drejtoj do t doja t siguroja Kuvendin e Shqipris, sistemin bankar, t gjith aktort e tjer t interesuar se Banka e Shqipris do t plotsoj nevojat e sistemit bankar me likuiditet. Nga ana tjetr, ne do t kmbngulim q sistemi bankar n politikat q aplikon n lidhje me tregun e paras dhe portofolin e investimeve t jet m i pavarur nga selit qendrore. Banka e Shqipris do t intensifikoj komunikimin me selit qendrore t bankave pr t mbshtetur financiarisht bijat e tyre q operojn n Shqipri. Bankat q operojn n Shqipri jan licencuar dhe administrojn kursimet e qytetarve shqiptar. Rrjedhimisht, obligimi themelor i do sistemi bankar sht ndrmjetsimi financiar n vendin ku ai operon. Pr kt arsye, ne do t kmbngulim q kreditimi i ekonomis t ringjallet duke sjell n vmendjen e sistemit degt e veanta t prodhimit q justifikojn mbshtetjen financiare t tij. Sistemi bankar duhet t jet m aktiv pr rifitimin e besimit publikut, nprmjet nj komunikimi n rritje dhe prezantimit t produkteve t reja q adresojn hezitimin e publikut. Komuniteti i biznesit duhet t hapet m shum ndaj sistemit bankar. Sinqeriteti i rritur dhe domosdoshmria pr t qen m vizionar n prcaktimin e planeve t ardhshme t biznesit, jan dy kushte t rndsishme pr ristabilizimin e kredis n parametra t dshiruar. Nj apel do t ju drejtoja edhe individve, qytetarve t thjesht. Mnyra se si ju silleni do dit prcakton edhe dinamikn e efekteve t krizs. Individt duhet t i kthehen bankave. Nse sjellja juaj do t jet racionale, ather dhe ndikimi i krizs do t jet periferik. Nse n sjelljen tuaj t prditshme z vend pseudofilozofia mikroproteksioniste e shfaqur n formn e panikut, mungess s besimit, largimit t depozitave nga bankat ather edhe mundsia pr t u prekur nga kriza financiare rritet m shum. Pr m tepr, mundsia pr t u shndrruar n nj kriz t ekonomis reale rritet. Sistemi financiar sht e vetmja makineri e specializuar q zotron informacionin, njohurit dhe burimet njerzore pr t br shprndarjen optimale t burimeve financiare n ekonomi. Prfitoj nga ky rast, t i drejtohem klass politike me nj thirrje pr rritjen e vmendjes ndaj sfidave me t cilat prballet vendi. Arritja e nj mirkuptimi politik n trajtimin e tyre do t reduktonte n koh dhe n intensitet efektet negative n ekonomi. Kt detyrim e kemi jo vetm ndaj vetes por edhe ndaj brezave t ardhshm, t cilt meritojn nj ambient m t prshtatshm biznesi, stabilitet makroekomik, sistem financiar t shndosh dhe perspektiv t qart konvergjence me Eurozonn. Kriza globale, tashm na i ka dhn msimet e para. Ajo na mson q na nevojitet m shum disiplin, m shum komunikim, m shum koordinim, m shum transparenc dhe m shum kultur. T nderuar zonja dhe zotrinj deputet, Stabiliteti makroekonomik i vendit ka amortizuar ndikimin e krizs ekonomike e financiare globale n aktivitetin ekonomik n vend. Ky stabilitet i shprehur n: inflacion t ult t mimeve t konsumit; qndrueshmri t bilancit t pagesave dhe t borxhit publik; bilance t shndosha t agjentve ekonomik; luhatje t ulta t tregut financiar; dhe besim t publikut n institucionet financiare, sht nj kapital i madh i ekonomis shqiptare. Ai sht prftuar me pun dhe sakrifica gjat viteve t shkuara, prandaj Banka e Shqipris gjykon se vmendja jon nuk duhet t shkputet nga ruajtja dhe konsolidimi i mtejshm i tij edhe n kto momente sfide pr t gjith ne. This important issue. The role of external anchors has been at the heart of our discussion Over the last three years. The Bank of Albania has discussed this issue in the context of possible future fiscal complications for monetary policy and the economy as a whole. I'll take a look at today's meeting, explain and discuss the ideas I have. forthe past two years. Albania makes up one of the success stories of the transition period supported by the International Monetary Fund's economic programmes. These programmes have been important anchors for sound macroeconomic and financial policies during most of the transition period. Structural reforms undertaken since the beginning of the transition period have brought significant progress in the political, economic and social aspects of the country, leading to significant increases in Albania's international image. As a result, the Strazburg Summit declared Albania a full member of NATO, and soon after this event, Albania submitted its official request to the next presidency of the European Union, the Czech Republic, to become a candidate for Membership in the European Union. The International Monetary Fund's last programme ended in January 2009, at the same time as the economic slowdown that followed the financial crisis in developed countries began to extend its influence on developing economies, including the Albanian economy. The same developments brought significant problems to central European economies. These recent problems in former countries with transitional economies, especially the successful economies of Central Europe, invite us to reflect on the role of institutions and the policies that have served as external anchors in this process. After the fall of communism, the International Monetary Fund was invited to draft and implement an economic programme that could transform former centralized economies into efficient market economies. Despite decreases and increases in economic results during the early stages of the transition period, along with several episodes of crises, the end of this period showed that the International Monetary Fund's supervisory programmes were successful in stabilizing transition economies and restoring overall macroeconomic balances. However, current events show that despite 20 years of reform, these economies remain fragile and sensitive to risks. In early 2000, many of these countries were preoccupied with the European Union membership process, and Maastrich's criteria turned into an important external poll for these economies. This process brought further consolidation of overall macroeconomic conditions. The new period, already as members of the European Union, was accompanied by rapid economic growth, widening the fiscal deficit and that of the current account. Fiscal consolidation changed direction and all economies showed signs of overheating. Significant capital inflows were financing all these activities and resulted in a steady increase in current account deficits. Instead of calming the economy, all these worrying developments were justified with the rapid process of approximation with the European Union. text: 06/08/2022, 09:17 During the presentation of economic developments in Albania and future challenges, organised by Citigroup London, IFC - Int... - Word of the Governor of the Bank of Albania Mr. Ardian Fullani, During the presentation of economic developments in Albania and future challenges, organised by Citigroup London, IFC - International Financial Services and the Embassy of the Republic of Albania in United Kingdom. May 18, 2009 Publication date: 22.05.2009  1/7 06/08/2022, 09:17 During the presentation of economic developments in Albania and future challenges, organised by Citigroup London, IFC - Int... Honored ladies and gentlemen! Let me start by thanking the Albanian Embassy here in London for organising this meeting. It is a pleasure for me to offer you a brief panorama on the latest trends and developments in the Albanian economy. Meetings of this kind are very important for confronting opportunities that provide a country with developing economies with the desire of developed countries for higher return. Our macroeconomic progress over the past few years, the sound banking system and our commitment to increasing its efficiency are the strengths with which I come before you today. The sound and stable economic and financial situation has been achieved through the implementation of a modern and visionary monetary policy, and as a result of a responsible fiscal policy. Macroeconomic success testifies to the ability of Albanian authorities to timely identify priorities, as well as to implement sound economic and social reforms. As a result, for the first time in 2007, Albania had its independent promotion in terms of its risk profile. The Moody Agency rated Albania with B, an assessment that was the same for 2008. In the last two years, our country has made a lot of progress towards the business climate, which is supported by a lot of data. I would like to mention here the World Bank Cost of Doing Business survey, which has climbed Albania from 135th to 86th place. For the first time in late 2007, Albania's public debt in the local currency was traded in international financial markets. Over the past few years, Albania has made a lot of improvements in the direction of the country's fiscal and monetary management. The implementation of the 10 percent flat tax was followed by a significant increase in tax collection. Recent improvements in legislation have contributed to the creation of a more favourable business climate. Some of the most important developments may be mentioned: the simplified tax setting system, their easier and less costly procedures; the best infrastructure for resolving related disputes; presentation of electronic tax procedures, as well as the reduction of the contribution to Social Security. It is also worth mentioning, the Bill for resolving administrative disputes in the Republic of Albania, which is in the discussion phase. This law will create administrative courts, which will have enough powers to judge on decisions made by Albanian fiscal authorities. The integration process has taken steps forward with two very important events. At the beginning of April this year, at the Strasbourg Summit, Albania became a member of NATO, while only ... i 2/7 06/08/2022, 09:17 During the presentation of economic developments in Albania and future challenges, organised by Citigroup London, IFC - Int... A few weeks later, our country presented the Czech Presidency with the official application for candidate status in the European Union. Thanks to its highly strategic geographical position, Albania has recently turned into a very important economic, political and stabilizing factor for the region. Characterized by these important geopolitical elements, Albania becomes a connecting bridge for Southeast Europe. Over the past decade, our country has been characterized by high and noninflationary economic growth, supported by domestic demand and driven by increased lending activity. In general, Albania has managed to keep prices under control, without affecting the country's growth or financial stability. Over the past few years, our country has recorded annual economic growth of 6 percent. Economic activity has increased sufficiently to cope with rapid growth in demand, contributing to keeping prices under control and anchoring inflationary expectations about the Bank of Albania's inflation target. Our target for maintaining the level of total inflation at 3 percent 1 percentage point has been successfully achieved. At the end of 2008, total consumer price inflation fluctuated to about 3 percent. Despite the moderate depreciation of the exchange rate during the first months of 2009, inflationary pressures have decreased in response to recent developments in international markets and economic contraction in our main trading partners, as well as slowing economic activity in the country. However, our estimates indicate that inflation for the following 12 months will remain within the tolerance interval. Our country has been characterized by continued fiscal consolidation over the past few years. The IMF presence has represented an important external complainant, thus promoting fiscal discipline. However, due to current ambitious projects to improve road infrastructure, capital expenditure has suffered increases, thus contributing to the expansion of the fiscal deficit in 2008. Major infrastructure projects have been financed, among other things, by revenues generated by privatisation of institutional sectors. Such a thing has contributed to the preservation of the government's public debt measure to the tune of 55 per cent of GDP, this acceptable measure taking into account the Maastricht Criteria. The exchange rate of the local currency, leku, is freely established in the currency market. The Bank of Albania believes that a free exchange rate regime is an important element in the process of correcting possible macroeconomic imbalances. The local currency has maintained stable levels starting in the 2000s. Also, the lek has shown a slight and continuous tendency of assessment, as a result of increasing productivity and a steady increase in income from immigrants. Starting in the year  3/7 06/08/2022, 09:17 During the presentation of economic developments in Albania and future challenges, organised by Citigroup London, IFC - Int... In 1998, the exchange rate fluctuated steadily. However, recent development trends, mainly in the foreign sector (falling incomes from immigrants and temporary expansion of the Korean account deficit), have contributed to the devaluation of the lec. By the end of April 2009, the effective nominal exchange rate suffered a decline of about 6 percent. Despite this, this devaluation remains at moderate levels, compared to the experience of other Central and Southeast European countries. Data on the balance of payments testify to increased confidence in the Albanian economy, mainly reflected in the addition of foreign direct investment, which in 2008 reached 6 percent of GDP. The current monetary policy framework can be considered an implicit regime of targeted inflation, managed through the use of indirect monetary policy instruments. Monetary policy signals are carried out through bank of Albania Supervisory Council decisions on the basic rate of week-long repurchase agreements, as well as through constant communication. Our country's natural resources, as well as the free but qualified labour force, are expected to be attractive elements for all European entrepreneurs, who want to explore the priorities that globalisation offers. The basis of exports ranges from agricultural products to those minerals. Albania offers a lot of investment opportunities in mining, agriculture, energy, infrastructure and tourism. The food processing industry is experiencing a satisfactory development, simultaneously creating many spaces for increased activity. While opportunities in the energy sector vary from building new resources, to improving the distribution network. Albania's strategic focus towards improving transport infrastructure requires greater public and private sector participation in building new roads and ports. As I mentioned above, our country offers extraordinary opportunities for investment in coastal, alpine, historical and cultural tourism, as a result of its favourable position in the Mediterranean, rich ethnographic heritage, as well as its changing climate and geology. Business culture enjoys great adaptive skills. The English language is well known to the younger generation. Albanians consider investment in their education to be quite important, while a significant number of young professionals have been educated in the United Kingdom and other European universities. With their education, they have developed Western working habits and represent valuable and helpful factors for expanding your business in the Balkan region. Not without purpose, I mentioned the region a little higher. Albania is no longer an isolated and lonely island of strange economic experiments. Over the past two decades, it has transformed into a free, flexible, competitive and open market to modern globalisation developments. Our country has learned to position itself properly and benefit from international developments in the region. Geographically, Albania is located in a key position, connecting the east with the west.  4/7 06/08/2022, 09:17 During the presentation of economic developments in Albania and future challenges, organised by Citigroup London, IFC - Int... As far as the financial system is concerned, our objective is to preserve a sound, cash and profitable system. At the end of 2008, the Albanian banking system consisted of 16 commercial banks. The privatisation of the banking system ended five years ago with the privatisation of the Savings Bank by Raiffeisen Bank. After that, in 2004, the percentage of private banks increased to 100 percent, where more than 90 percent of shareholder capital is foreign. Over the past few years, credit for the private sector and individuals has increased significantly. Undoubtedly, lending has been a supporting factor for economic growth and investment in the country. The banking sector stands at the forefront of foreign direct investment and the country's integration process. It represents one of the most successful investment opportunities in Albania, benefiting greatly from the presence of some of the largest financial groups in Europe. My reference to integration refers not only to the presence of foreign capital, but also to the capacity of the banking system to mediate and complement European initiatives and investments in the Albanian economy. These banks enjoy the reputation, ability and infrastructure needed to serve as partners for foreign investors. The banking system is necessary, but not a sufficient condition to promote economic well-being and realize the distribution of resources to the best possible users. The distribution of the financial market in Albania is annoyed by universal commercial banks. Other types like joint funds, high-risk investment companies, pension funds and investment banks do not exist. The Bank of Albania and other market financial authorities are encouraging the creation of appropriate incentives for the promotion of investments in these segments. We believe that our financial system has not yet exploited all its possibilities. Taking advantage of this meeting, I would like to invite all British companies to include Albania on their investment map. Honored ladies and gentlemen! Global developments have dominated the agenda of decision-makers worldwide. So far, the Albanian economy has shown admirable resistance to these developments. Macroeconomic and financial stability have been achieved and the banking system remains secular. However, the effects of the international financial crisis appeared on the Albanian economy starting in the last quarter of 2008. The first consequence was the withdrawal of deposits, reflecting the decline in public confidence in the banking system. The main causes that prompted the withdrawal of deposits in mid-October 2008 are thought to be limited recognition of real problems, reinforced by reports from migrant relatives in Italy and Greece, which prompted panic in public.  5/7 06/08/2022, 09:17 During the presentation of economic developments in Albania and future challenges, organised by Citigroup London, IFC - Int... Another notable consequence is the decrease in incoming currency flows, in the form of income from immigrants and exports of goods and services, which tightened the overall financial situation in the economy, putting pressure on the exchange rate. At this point, the Bank of Albania began to assess the situation, with the aim of preparing for the effects of the second round, which would come as a result of the tightening of the liquidity situation and the global situation, which was already facing an economic recession. The Bank of Albania has communicated its concerns regarding the indirect impact of the financial crisis, listing the possible effects of the second round that will exert stronger pressures during 2009: We expect the tightening of the liquidity situation to slow lending growth and economic growth. The expected slowdown in our exports and lower commodity prices will lead to an increase in the trade deficit. Also, further reduction in income from immigrants will contribute to the increase in the Korean account deficit. However, we believe that the free exchange rate regime will be an effective instrument for regulating consumption and consequently imports. The Bank of Albania will not intervene for fixing any price on the market. As always, she will try to avoid any pronounced disorder in the market. The fiscal deficit is expected to increase, as a result of an expected negative impact of economic activity on budgetary income and their financing, due to the tightening of the liquidity situation in national and international markets. Our analyses show that economic activity will slow significantly. However, it will remain at positive levels. Stress-test analyses show that the quality of the loan portfolio is expected to deteriorate further, as a result of slowing economic activity, exchange rate depreciation, as well as the statistical effect of lower lending growth. However, the quality of this portfolio will remain within acceptable borders and is not expected to significantly threaten the country's financial stability. Also, the Bank of Albania's short-term target shifted towards maintaining stability and minimising the effects of the second round, keeping in constant attention developments in inflation, which has shifted to the fallen direction. Honored participants, The year we face will be difficult. There are a lot of challenges ahead of us. Combining the financial crisis with the global economic recession is an unprecient case. My country, Albania, is also part of this global picture. So far, we have managed to preserve both economic and financial stability. We remain committed to further preserving these achievements. Thanking you for your attention, I remain open to any questions.  6/7 06/08/2022, 09:17 During the presentation of economic developments in Albania and future challenges, organised by Citigroup London, IFC - Int...  7/7

Ardian Fullani, Gjat prezantimit t zhvillimeve ekonomike n Shqipri dhe sfidave t ardhshme, organizuar nga Citigroup Londr, IFC - International Financial Services dhe Ambasadn e Republiks s Shqipris n Mbretrin e Bashkuar. 18 maj 2009 Data e publikimit: 22.05.2009 https://www.bankofalbania.org/Shtypi/Fjalime_intervista_artikuj/Fjalime/Gjate_prezantimit_te_zhvillimeve_ekonomike_ne_Shqiperi_dhe_sfidave_t 1/7 06/08/2022, 09:17 Gjat prezantimit t zhvillimeve ekonomike n Shqipri dhe sfidave t ardhshme, organizuar nga Citigroup Londr, IFC - Int T nderuar zonja dhe zotrinj! M lejoni t filloj duke falenderuar Ambasadn e Shqipris ktu n Londr pr organizimin e ktij takimi. sht nj knaqsi pr mua q tju ofroj nj panoram t shkurtr mbi tendencat dhe zhvillimet m t fundit n ekonomin shqiptare. Takime t ktij lloji jan mjaft t rndsishme pr ballafaqimin e mundsive q ofron nj vend me ekonomi n zhvillim me dshirn e vendeve t zhvilluara pr kthim m t lart. Progresi yn makroekonomik gjat viteve t fundit, sistemi i shndosh bankar dhe angazhimi yn pr rritjen e eficiencs s tij jan pikat e forta me t cilat un vij sot prpara jush. Gjendja e shndosh dhe e qndrueshme ekonomike dhe financiare sht arritur prmes zbatimit t nj politike monetare moderne dhe vizionare, dhe si rezultat i nj politike t prgjegjshme fiskale. Suksesi makroekonomik dshmon pr aftsin e autoriteteve shqiptare pr identifikimin n kohn e duhur t prioriteteve, si dhe pr zbatimin e reformave t shndosha ekonomike dhe shoqrore. Si rezultat, pr her t par n vitin 2007, Shqipria pati gradimin e saj t pavarur lidhur me profilin e rrezikut t saj. Agjencia Moody e vlersoi Shqiprin me B+, vlersim i cili ishte i njjt edhe pr vitin 2008. N dy vitet e fundit, vendi yn ka br mjaft progres n drejtim t klims s biznesit, fakt i cili mbshtetet nga mjaft t dhna. Do t doja t prmendja ktu anketn e Banks Botrore  Cost of Doing Business (T bsh biznes), e cila e ka ngjitur Shqiprin nga vendi i 135-t n at t 86-t. Pr her t par n fund t vitit 2007, borxhi publik i Shqipris n monedhn vendase u tregtua n tregjet financiare ndrkombtare. Gjat viteve t fundit, Shqipria ka br mjaft prmirsime n drejtim t administrimit fiskal dhe monetar t vendit. Zbatimi i takss s shesht prej 10 pr qind u pasua nga nj rritje e konsiderueshme n mbledhjen e taksave. Prmirsimet e fundit n legjislacion kan kontribuuar n krijimin e nj klime m t favorshme biznesi. Disa nga zhvillimet m kryesore mund t prmenden: sistemi i thjeshtuar i vendosjes s taksave, procedurat m t lehta dhe m pak t kushtueshme t tyre; infrastruktura m e mir pr zgjidhjen e mosmarrveshjeve lidhur me to; prezantimi i procedurave elektronike pr taksat, si dhe ulja e kontributit pr sigurimin shoqror. Vlen t prmendet gjithashtu, projektligji pr zgjidhjen e mosmarrveshjeve administrative n Republikn e Shqipris, i cili sht n faz diskutimi. Ky ligj do krijoj gjykata administrative, t cilat do t ken mjaft kompetenca pr t gjykuar mbi vendimet e marra nga autoritetet fiskale shqiptare. Procesi i integrimit ka br hapa prpara me dy ngjarje mjaft t rndsishme. N fillim t muajit prill t ktij viti, n Samitin e Strasburgut, Shqipria u b antare e NATO-s, ndrkoh q vetm https://wkwwj .bankofalbania.org/Shtypi/dFjialime_initervista_aritikiuPj/Fjalimide/Gjate_prezanktimit_te_lzihkviillimieve_ekonomike_ne_Shqipeiri_dhek_sfidadvied_ti 2/7 06/08/2022, 09:17 Gjat prezantimit t zhvillimeve ekonomike n Shqipri dhe sfidave t ardhshme, organizuar nga Citigroup Londr, IFC - Int pak jav m von, vendi yn i paraqiti Presidencs eke aplikimin zyrtar pr statusin e kandidatit n Bashkimin Evropian. Fal pozicionit t saj gjeografik mjaft strategjik, Shqipria sht shndrruar koht e fundit n nj faktor mjaft i rndsishm ekonomik, politik dhe stabilizues pr rajonin. E karakterizuar nga kto elemente t rndsishme gjeopolitike, Shqipria bhet ur lidhse pr Evropn Juglindore. Gjat dekads s fundit, vendi yn sht karakterizuar nga nj rritje ekonomike e lart dhe joinflacioniste, e mbshtetur nga krkesa e brendshme dhe e nxitur nga rritja e aktivitetit kreditues. N prgjithsi, Shqipria ka arritur t mbaj mimet nn kontroll, pa cnuar rritjen apo stabilitetin financiar t vendit. Gjat viteve t fundit, vendi yn ka regjistruar nj rritje ekonomike vjetore prej 6 pr qind. Aktiviteti ekonomik sht rritur n mnyr t mjaftueshme pr t prballuar rritjen e shpejt t krkess, duke kontribuar n mbajtjen e mimeve nn kontroll dhe n ankorimin e pritjeve inflacioniste rreth objektivit t Banks s Shqipris pr inflacionin. Objektivi yn pr ruajtjen e nivelit t inflacionit total n 3 pr qind  1 pik prqindjeje sht arritur n mnyr t suksesshme. N fund t vitit 2008, inflacioni total i mimeve t konsumit u luhat n rreth 3 pr qind. Pavarsisht zhvlersimit t moderuar t kursit t kmbimit gjat muajve t par t vitit 2009, presionet inflacioniste jan ulur n prgjigje t zhvillimeve t fundit n tregjet ndrkombtare dhe tkurrjes ekonomike n partnert tan kryesor tregtar, si dhe t ngadalsimit t aktivitetit ekonomik n vend. Megjithat, vlersimet tona tregojn se inflacioni pr 12 muajt n vijim do t mbetet brenda intervalit t tolerancs. Vendi yn sht karakterizuar nga nj konsolidim i vazhdueshm fiskal gjat viteve t fundit. Prania e FMN-s ka prfaqsuar nj ankor t rndsishme t jashtme, duke nxitur kshtu disiplinn fiskale. Megjithat, pr shkak t projekteve aktuale ambicioze pr prmirsimin e infrastrukturs rrugore, shpenzimet kapitale kan psuar rritje, duke kontribuar kshtu n zgjerimin e deficitit fiskal n vitin 2008. Projektet e mdha infrastrukturore jan financuar ndrmjet t tjerash, nga t ardhurat e realizuara nga privatizimi i sektorve institucional. Nj gj e till, ka kontribuar n ruajtjen e mass s borxhit publik t qeveris n masn 55 pr qind t PBB-s, mas kjo e pranueshme duke marr parasysh Kriteret e Mastrihtit. Kursi i kmbimit t monedhs vendase, lekut, sht vendosur lirisht n tregun valutor. Banka e Shqipris beson se nj regjim i lir i kursit t kmbimit sht nj element i rndsishm n procesin e korrektimit t zhbalancimeve t mundshme makroekonomike. Monedha vendase ka ruajtur nivele t qndrueshme duke filluar nga vitet 2000. Gjithashtu, leku ka shfaqur nj tendenc t leht dhe t vazhdueshme vlersimi, si rezultat i rritjes s produktivitetit dhe shtimit t qndrueshm t t ardhurave nga emigrantt.
